# apim_catalog_mcp_server (Resource)

CatalogMcpServer Resource

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "github_mcp_authorization" {
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  description = "Full value of the Authorization header, such as \"Bearer <token>\""
}

resource "apim_catalog_mcp_server" "github" {
  hrid        = "github"
  entity_id   = "mcp-server.github"
  description = "GitHub tools for coding agents"
  server_connection = {
    endpoint = "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/"
    auth = {
      header = {
        name  = "Authorization"
        value = var.github_mcp_authorization
      }
    }
  }
}

# The platform discovers the server when it is applied. Its tools come back in
# the state, each with the entity id an authorization policy names.
output "github_tools" {
  value = apim_catalog_mcp_server.github.tools
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `entity_id` (String) Stable catalog identity of the server, the name authorization policies reference: lowercase, dot-separated
segments, first segment `mcp-server`. Validated, never repaired: an invalid value, or a value already used by
another server of the environment, is rejected. Immutable once the server exists — declaring a different value
is rejected rather than applied, since nothing re-points the policies naming the old one. Delete the server and
declare it again to give it another identity.
- `hrid` (String) A unique human readable id identifying this resource. Requires replacement if changed.
- `server_connection` (Attributes) How the platform reaches the upstream MCP server (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--server_connection))

### Optional

- `description` (String) Human description shown in the Catalog
- `environment_id` (String) environment ID
- `organization_id` (String) organization ID

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Resource UUID
- `last_synced_at` (String) When the server's tools, prompts and resources were last synced; a registered server has synced at least once
- `prompts` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--prompts))
- `protocol_version` (String) MCP protocol version negotiated with the server
- `resources` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resources))
- `server_info` (Attributes) What the server said about itself when it was discovered (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--server_info))
- `tools` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tools))

<a id="nestedatt--server_connection"></a>
### Nested Schema for `server_connection`

Required:

- `auth` (Attributes) Authentication the platform uses against the upstream MCP server, discriminated by `type`. Credential values are
stored verbatim: a literal, or a `secret://` URI pointing at a configured secret provider. They are never returned
by this API, and a spec that omits a credential clears the stored one. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--server_connection--auth))
- `endpoint` (String) URL of the upstream MCP server, http or https

Optional:

- `transport` (String) MCP transport of the upstream server; `HTTP` is the streamable HTTP transport, the only one discovery supports today. Default: "HTTP"; must be "HTTP"

<a id="nestedatt--server_connection--auth"></a>
### Nested Schema for `server_connection.auth`

Optional:

- `header` (Attributes) A static header sent on every request. Write the full header value: `Bearer <token>` for a bearer token,
`Basic <base64>` for basic credentials, or the raw key for an API-key header — or point the whole value at a
secret with a `secret://` URI. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--server_connection--auth--header))
- `none` (Attributes) No authentication (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--server_connection--auth--none))
- `oauth2` (Attributes) OAuth 2.0 client credentials; the platform fetches a token from `tokenUrl` before reaching the server (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--server_connection--auth--oauth2))

<a id="nestedatt--server_connection--auth--header"></a>
### Nested Schema for `server_connection.auth.header`

Required:

- `name` (String) Header name
- `value` (String, Sensitive) Full header value, a literal or a `secret://` URI stored verbatim; never returned

Optional:

- `type` (String) Type of authentication. Default: "HEADER"; must be "HEADER"


<a id="nestedatt--server_connection--auth--none"></a>
### Nested Schema for `server_connection.auth.none`

Optional:

- `type` (String) Type of authentication. Default: "NONE"; must be "NONE"


<a id="nestedatt--server_connection--auth--oauth2"></a>
### Nested Schema for `server_connection.auth.oauth2`

Required:

- `client_id` (String) OAuth 2.0 client id
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) OAuth 2.0 client secret, a literal or a `secret://` URI stored verbatim; never returned
- `token_url` (String) Token endpoint of the authorization server

Optional:

- `scope` (String) Space-separated scopes requested with the token
- `type` (String) Type of authentication. Default: "OAUTH2"; must be "OAUTH2"

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = apim_catalog_mcp_server.github
  id = jsonencode({
    environment_id  = "DEFAULT"
    hrid            = "github"
    organization_id = "DEFAULT"
  })
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import apim_catalog_mcp_server.github '{"environment_id": "DEFAULT", "hrid": "github", "organization_id": "DEFAULT"}'
```
